newsitem.title: USA: Stone Energy sees December South Pelto test.
newsitem.headline: Stone Energy sees December South Pelto test.

text.p: Stone Energy Corp said on Monday it expects to test "a significant discovery well" drilled in the South Pelto Block 23 Field, located in federal waters offshore Louisiana.
It said two additional wells are planned for the first half of 1997 to further delineate the extent of the discovery.

Analysis of electric logs from the OCS-G No. 24 Well indicates about 400 net feet of pay in multiple reservoirs in the 18,002 foot well confirming the presence of a productive structure in a previously untested area of the block which was interpreted from 3-D seismic, the company said.

First production from this discovery is expected by the fourth quarter of 1997, it continued, adding the design of the "D" Platform and facilities to produce from the new area is currently in progress.
About 3,800 feet southwest of the No. 24 Well, the company has completed and tested the previously announced No. 22 Well at South Pelto Block 23, it said.

On limited test, the well flowed at the average daily rates of 450 barrels of oil and 2.5 million cubic feet of gas with flowing tubing pressure of 5,780 pounds per square inch on a 10/64-inch choke. The No. 22 Well will produce from the newly constructed "C" Platform, and first production is planned for February 1997, Stone said.
The company owns a 98 percent working interest in the block. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
